title: Minimum Falling Path Sum II
summary: For an n x n integer matrix grid, find the minimum sum of a falling path with non-zero shifts.
statement: For an n x n integer matrix grid, find the minimum sum of a falling path with non-zero shifts. A falling path with non-zero shifts is defined as selecting exactly one element from each row such that no two elements chosen in adjacent rows are from the same column.
constraints: grid is a nonempty square matrix.
Choose one value from each row; adjacent choices must use different columns.
Return the minimum possible total, including negative values.
hints: Let each column store the best total ending there in the previous row.
For a new column, add the smallest prior total from a different column.
Track the smallest and second-smallest prior columns to make each transition constant time.
Every valid path has one previous column; the recurrence minimizes over exactly those allowed predecessors.
editorial: Dynamic programming keeps the best total ending in each column. Only the smallest previous total is needed unless it comes from the forbidden same column, in which case the second-smallest is used. This produces each row in linear time. The oracle independently checks every other previous column for every transition.

tests.explanation: Choosing one, five, and seven uses different adjacent columns and totals thirteen.
The only one-row path has sum seven.
